True Statement: Over a million species of animals have been described till now.
False 1: Over a hundred thousand species of animals have been described till now.

True Statement: Animals have fundamental features common in relation to the arrangement of cells, body symmetry, nature of coelom, patterns of digestive, circulatory or reproductive systems.
False 1: Animals have fundamental features common in relation to the arrangement of cells, body symmetry, nature of coelom, patterns of digestive, circulatory or nervous systems.

True Statement: All members of Animalia are multicellular.
False 1: All members of Animalia are unicellular.

True Statement: In sponges, the cells are arranged as loose cell aggregates, exhibiting cellular level of organisation.
False 1: In coelenterates, the cells are arranged as loose cell aggregates, exhibiting cellular level of organisation.

True Statement: Sponges are mostly asymmetrical — any plane that passes through the centre does not divide them into equal halves.

True Statement: The animals in which the body cavity is absent are called acoelomates, e.g., platyhelminthes.

True Statement: In earthworm, the body shows metameric segmentation and the phenomenon is known as metamerism.

True Statement: Annelids may be aquatic (marine and fresh water) or terrestrial; free-living, and sometimes parasitic.
False 1: Annelids are exclusively aquatic and cannot be terrestrial.
